title: Add without overflowing
hints: You can't compute `a + b` first and check afterwards: if it overflows, the damage (undefined behavior) is already done. Decide *before* adding, using only operations that can't overflow.

Overflow upwards is only possible when `b > 0`, and it happens exactly when `a > INT_MAX - b`. Downwards only when `b < 0`, exactly when `a < INT_MIN - b`. Both subtractions are safe given the sign of `b`.

For subtraction, don't rewrite it as `checked_add(a, -b, out)`: `-INT_MIN` overflows. Mirror the add checks instead: `b < 0 && a > INT_MAX + b` overflows up, `b > 0 && a < INT_MIN + b` overflows down.
